The G-code simulator is complete and runs at `output/main.py` using only the Python standard library. 

## Summary

The simulator is split across 7 modules in `output/`:
- **`main.py`** — CLI entry point, argument parsing, and orchestration
- **`gparser.py`** — Line preprocessing, expression evaluator, parser → Block
- **`state.py`** — Machine state, modal groups, parameters, units, coordinate systems
- **`canon.py`** — Path geometry (linear, arcs, helices), state snapshots, delta computation
- **`simulator.py`** — Block executor implementing Table 8 ordering, all G/M codes, canned cycles, CRC, probing
- **`tracer.py`** — Trace builder with the three stepping modes (time / distance / position-tolerance)
- **`files.py`** — Tool table and parameter file readers/writer

Verified against all three prompt examples plus extensive testing:
- Linear motion with time stepping → matches example 1 exactly (0.5 / 1.0 entries)
- G81 canned cycle expansion with distance stepping → matches example 2 exactly (4 sub-motions, motion_kind labels, time 3.72 cumulative)
- G43 H99 error case → exit 1, error_line_number=2, partial entries preserved
- Expression evaluation, G2/G3 arcs (radius and center format, full circles, all 3 planes), G91 incremental, G92 offsets, G93 inverse-time, G87 back-boring, G84 spindle-reverse with trailing-entry semantics, G38.2 probing with `--probe-box`, M2/M30 program-end resets, percent demarcation, block delete, parameter file round-trip, tool table loading, units conversion (G20/G21).
